_comment: Spec consumed by scripts/gen-ci-workflow.py. The `jobs` map lists the make-invocation block of each correspondingly-named job in .github/workflows/test.yml (one marker-bounded generated region per job; the job scaffolding — checkout, composite setup, cache saves, artifact upload — stays hand-written). Every generated step gets `!cancelled()` merged into its condition so one red gate never hides its siblings (detector-not-gate CI: results are read after the fact, so a run must surface every failure at once). Add a new gate by appending to the right job here and running scripts/gen-ci-workflow.py; the make test-integration-lint-ci-workflow target fails CI if this spec disagrees with the on-disk workflow.
_coverage_comment: ci_coverage_exceptions / ci_coverage_known_holes feed scripts/check-ci-gate-coverage.py (make test-integration-lint-ci-coverage): every test-unit/test-integration/test-e2e/test-coverage aggregator leaf must run in some workflow, be a named exception (permanent, reason required), or be a known hole (temporary; warns, and the lint fails if a hole becomes covered without being removed here).

ci_coverage_exceptions.test-e2e-jupyter: dep-chains jupyter-install into a full backend rebuild; run locally when touching the kernel

lint-full.name: Typecheck torch_ref (pyright)
comment: Alias of ref-typecheck: pyright over packages/pytorch/torch_ref/
at the typeCheckingMode pinned in its pyproject.toml. Lives in
this venv-bearing lint job (not the dep-free `lint` job) because
import resolution needs the full uv venv from ref-setup.
Pyright version is pinned by uv.lock.

lint-full.name: Typecheck idris-ml-examples Python helpers (pyright strict)
comment: pyright strict over packages/idris-ml-examples/scripts/ (config
root: its pyrightconfig.json, selected via -p). verify_dtypes.py
imports torch/safetensors, which only the full ref-setup venv
carries.

lint-full.name: Typecheck idris-transformers scripts (pyright strict)
comment: pyright strict over packages/idris-transformers/scripts/ (config
root: its pyrightconfig.json via -p). The oracle/compare scripts
import torch/transformers/safetensors, which only the full
ref-setup venv carries.

lint-full.name: Full clang-tidy over torch C++ backend (advisory)
comment: The default `lint-c` runs clang-tidy on tape only; the torch
C++ sources need libtorch headers, which this job carries for
free via the ref-setup venv (the Makefile's LIBTORCH_PATH
detection finds the venv's torch). Closes the long-deferred
"full clang-tidy needs libtorch staged" follow-up. Advisory
until the first run's findings are triaged — the torch C++
tree has never been clang-tidy'd and can't be linted locally
(macOS+nix clang-tidy rejects Apple SDK headers); promote by
dropping continue-on-error once clean.

test-unit.name: Run idris-gym unit suite
comment: Pure-Idris suite for the gym package (spaces, RNG, classic-control
+ toy-text envs, wrappers) via the pack-built test harness. Wired
in by the gate-coverage lint — it was the only test-unit leaf
running in no workflow.

test-unit.name: Run idris-transformers unit tests
comment: Pure-Idris test harness for the HF-aligned model package
(packages/idris-transformers/): bertParamNames catalogue + an FFI
suite that constructs a real HfBert and asserts the C-side param
registry matches the catalogue.

test-unit.name: Run examples unit suite (tape)
comment: Idris-side suite living in packages/idris-ml-examples (Test.Reinforce,
Test.Generate). Wired in to catch drift like the IO-lift mismatch on
rolloutEpBatched and the bitlinear-test scale formula — both pre-existed
in tree because the target was not previously gated by CI.

test-unit.name: Run Idris unit suite (tape)
comment: Idris-side smart-constructor / LayerLike / Tensor-lifecycle suite
against the tape primary. The test buckets that touch the C
surface (GradMode, ManagedHandle) use `{d=TestExecutor}` which the
Makefile-generated `TestConfig.idr` resolves to TapeExecutor here, so
FFI calls land on tape-suffixed C symbols.

test-unit.name: Run Idris unit suite (torch, Ubuntu)
comment: Same suite as the tape lane but with TestExecutor = TorchExecutor TCpu.
Catches Idris-side regressions that a tape-only run would miss
(broken torch Scheme wrapper, drift in `UserExecutorTransfer`
instances, etc.).

test-unit.name: Run Idris unit suite (mlx, macOS)
comment: Same suite as tape/torch but with TestExecutor = MlxExecutor MCpu.
Catches mlx Scheme-wrapper drift, lazy-eval / handle-lifetime
regressions in the test-managed-handle suite under Metal.

test-unit.name: Run multi-backend Idris suite (macOS)
comment: Adds Test.Transfer (cross-backend `toExecutor` smoke) +
Test.MultiExecutorRegistry (registry isolation invariant) on
top of the per-backend buckets. Forces BACKEND=torch,tape,mlx
so all three sets of C symbols are linked — only feasible on
the macOS lane (Ubuntu has no mlx).

test-unit.name: Full clang-tidy over mlx C++ backend (macOS, advisory)
comment: The default `lint-c` runs clang-tidy on tape only; the mlx C++
sources need the MLX headers, which only this macOS lane stages
(MLX_SITE from the composite). brew's clang-tidy is installed by
the scaffolding step above. Advisory: the mlx tree has never
been clang-tidy'd, and the Apple-SDK-vs-llvm pre-include skew
that blocks nix clang-tidy locally may produce FPs here too —
promote by dropping continue-on-error once a run comes back
clean.

test-unit.name: Run Criterion suite under ASan + UBSan (tape, Ubuntu)
comment: AddressSanitizer + UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer pass over the
C tape backend + Criterion suite. The Makefile target sets
EXTRA_CFLAGS='-fsanitize=address,undefined ...' on top of the
stock -O2 build and lands the artifacts in a distinct
`build/<key>-asan/` tree (via the ASAN axis in BUILD_KEY)
so the warm tree stays clean.
First runs may surface latent UB sites — `continue-on-error:
true` keeps this advisory until the first cleanup commits
land; promote to hard-fail by dropping that line. mlx + torch
lanes are deferred (mlx-Metal + asan interactions are messy;
libtorch + asan is supported but slow to set up).
Ubuntu-only because asan on macOS requires a separate
instrumented runtime and clang invocation.

test-integration.name: Verify GradMode gate (NoGrad loss rejected at compile)
comment: Asserts the type-level gate `nativeTrainStep : ... -> Tensor [] d
WithGrad -> Double` still rejects a `NoGrad` loss. If this step
ever passes the negative test (i.e. the gate compiles a NoGrad
loss), the "inference loss silently no-ops training" bug class
has regressed.

test-integration.name: Verify GradMode aliasing rejection (linear freezeNetwork)
comment: Asserts that linear `freezeNetwork` consumes its input — using
the pre-freeze Network reference afterwards must be a compile
error. Prevents the "freeze net, train via original variable
which silently no-ops" footgun.

test-integration.name: Verify cross-family lossless-cast gate (DType.Core.LosslessTo)
comment: Asserts LosslessTo refuses a mantissa-shrinking direction
(F32 to BF16). Prevents silent precision-losing mid-graph
casts. Pairs with the positive Test.Lossless suite.

test-integration.name: Verify int-overflow lossless-cast gate (#412 F1)
comment: Asserts LosslessTo refuses I64 to F32 (max int value far
exceeds F32 mantissa exact-integer ceiling). Pairs with the
I32 to F64 + U8 to F32 positive cases in Test.Lossless.

test-integration.name: Type-check HfLlamaInference example
comment: `idris2 --check` over Example/HfLlamaInference.idr — the example
is too heavy to *run* outside the dedicated roundtrip gates, but
type-drift against the library surface is cheap to catch here.
Wired in by the gate-coverage lint.

test-integration.name: Run typed index-op round-trip (torch, Ubuntu)
comment: Verifies the typed targsort/tgather/tscatterAdd surface *resolves*
on torch (Compatible d I64) and runs — the C test covers numerics,
check-all is tape-only and can't resolve the I64 gate. Torch-only:
an integer-dtyped index tensor exists nowhere else.

test-integration.name: Run coverage gap probe (advisory)
comment: Static probe: parses OP_* enums from backend_<b>/tape.h and
extern "C" decls from backend.h, cross-references against
test/. Writes CSVs to build/coverage-gap-{ops,symbols}.csv.
Exit code is advisory today (0 even on gaps); coverage-policy.md
flips this to gating once W3+W4 close. See
docs/develop/coverage-policy.md for the three-axis target.

test-integration.name: Checkpoint resume smoke test
comment: Trains gpt 10 epochs to a checkpoint dir, resumes to 20, and
asserts the sidecar epoch + resume log + completion. Gates the
Train.idr / Checkpoint.idr auto-save / resume integration.

test-e2e-examples.name: Run example smoke matrix
comment: Every example across the backend lanes available on this runner
(tape + torch on Ubuntu; tape + mlx on macOS), few-epoch smoke
thresholds. No SKIP_EXAMPLES: the mlx allocator aborts that used
to skip ntm-copy / ntm-associative-recall / dnc-recall /
mountain-car-cont are fixed by the generation-scoped free (see
docs/develop/tensor-lifecycle.md).

test-e2e-hf.name: Run PyTorch reference correctness suite
comment: pytest over packages/pytorch/torch_ref/correctness/ — the
PyTorch side is the correctness oracle for every paired example,
so its own suite gates first. Wired in by the gate-coverage
lint — it ran in no workflow despite being the oracle.

test-e2e-hf.name: Run RoPE table oracle
comment: Generates the Llama-3 RoPE table oracle (inv_freq + cos/sin
slice) consumed by the Idris-side RoPE tests.

test-e2e-hf.name: Run HfBert oracle generator + pytest
comment: Drives packages/idris-transformers/scripts/save_oracle.py through
pytest under the pytorch uv venv (carries the transformers dep).
Downloads google/bert_uncased_L-2_H-128_A-2 from HF Hub, runs
forward on the fixed input, asserts the resulting oracle is
shape [128] F32 finite + non-trivial.

test-e2e-hf.name: Run HfGpt2 oracle generator + pytest
comment: Same shape as the HfBert oracle gate but for sshleifer/tiny-gpt2.
Downloads the checkpoint, runs forward on [15496, 995], asserts
the last-position hidden state is shape [2] (sshleifer/tiny-gpt2
is intentionally degenerate at hidden=2 — exercises the
architectural pieces without burning CI disk).

test-e2e-hf.name: Run HfLlama oracle generator + pytest
comment: Oracle-generation pytest for unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B. Wired in by
the gate-coverage lint (the roundtrip regenerates the oracle
anyway, but this gate asserts the generator script's own
invariants and fails earlier + cheaper).

test-e2e-hf.name: Run HfLlama generation oracle pytest
comment: Greedy-decode oracle pytest paired with the llama-generate
roundtrip below. Wired in by the gate-coverage lint.

test-e2e-hf.name: Run HfBert end-to-end roundtrip
comment: The cross-language correctness gate: regenerates the Python
oracle, runs the Idris HfBertInference example (loading the
real Google bert-tiny weights via the HF-aligned HfBert
module), and asserts elementwise agreement within
max-abs-diff 1e-3 on the 128-dim pooled [CLS] output.
Currently passes at 4.1e-4 locally on tape.

test-e2e-hf.name: Run HfGpt2 end-to-end roundtrip
comment: Same gate shape as HfBert but for GPT-2: regenerate the Python
oracle from hf-internal-testing/tiny-random-gpt2, run the Idris
HfGpt2Inference binary, assert the 32-dim last-position hidden
state matches within max-abs-diff 1e-3. Currently passes at
~1e-6 locally on tape.

test-e2e-hf.name: Run HfBitNet end-to-end roundtrip (torch)
comment: Cross-language gate: regenerate the Python oracle from
microsoft/bitnet-b1.58-2B-4T, run the Idris HfBitNetInference
binary --dump-logits, assert argmax on the vocab-128256 logit
row matches the HF oracle at max-abs-diff 1.0. BACKEND=torch
because tape F64 on a ~2B-param model OOMs the 14 GB Ubuntu
runner (see Low-priority TODO "Tape F64 large-LM OOM"). BitNet
is not license-gated, so no HF_TOKEN handling needed. The
job-level swapfile absorbs the cold-tree elaboration peak that
OOM-killed run 27364532457.

test-e2e-hf.name: Run HfLlama end-to-end roundtrip (torch)
comment: Cross-language gate for Llama 3.2 1B. Regenerates the Python
oracle from unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B (public mirror of Meta's
weights, no license-gate / no HF_TOKEN), runs the Idris
HfLlamaInference binary --dump-final-hidden, asserts the
2048-dim last-position hidden state matches the oracle within
max-abs-diff 1.0. Currently passes at 4.96e-05 on torch-mps
and 1.20e-04 on mlx-gpu in local dev runs; the CI torch-cpu
lane carries the same Idris-side numerics through libtorch CPU.
BACKEND=torch because tape F64 doesn't fit (~10 GB params +
arena vs ~14 GB runner RAM); see Low-priority TODO "Tape F64
large-LM OOM".

test-e2e-hf.name: Run HfLlama multi-step generation roundtrip (torch)
comment: Cross-language gate for Llama 3.2 1B's *generation* path.
The companion single-forward gate above tests one fixed token;
this step exercises the full greedy-decode loop: tokenize "The
capital of France is", generate 4 tokens via `genLoop` (no KV
cache yet — bumps to 8+ once KV cache lands), assert the
resulting token-ID sequence matches HF `model.generate(
do_sample=False, use_cache=True)` element-wise. Catches drift
in tokenization, every layer of the forward, argmax, and the
per-step glue that the single-forward gate can't see.
